raw:
[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old English fenn (fen, marsh) + weg (way, path); Middle English fenne + wey",
    "reading": "The path through the marsh; a raised way crossing wet ground.",
    "languages": ["en", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. fen, way",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Fen + way; fen (marsh) + way (route); also 'fen' as in 'fence' (enclosure) + 'way'",
    "reading": "The enclosed route; a passage bounded by barriers, a corridor of limits.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fen (fr. 'fen' = hay) + way (en. path); 'fen' in Dutch = marsh; 'way' in Old Norse = veig (strength)",
    "reading": "Hay-path or marsh-strength; a route of harvest or of boggy power.",
    "languages": ["fr", "nl", "non"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Fenway -> 'we fan y' -> 'y we fan' -> 'fan wey' (fan = winnower, wey = weight/measure)",
    "reading": "The winnower's measure; a weighing of chaff and grain on the path.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "F-E-N-W-A-Y: Fons Et Numen Via Aquae Ylem — 'source and spirit, way of water and matter'",
    "reading": "A sacred waterway; the path where spirit and primal substance meet.",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "F (fire, 6) + E (breath, 5) + N (water, 14) + W (double U, 23) + A (air, 1) + Y (Yggdrasil, 25)",
    "reading": "Fire, breath, water, double-void, air, and world-tree — a cosmic crossroads.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "F=6, E=5, N=14, W=23, A=1, Y=25; sum = 74; 7+4=11; 1+1=2",
    "reading": "Reduces to 11 (master number) then 2 — duality, reflection, the path between two worlds.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old English fenn + weg; also compare Old Norse fen (mire) + vegr (road)",
    "reading": "The mire-road; a causeway through treacherous ground, a liminal crossing.",
    "languages": ["en", "non"],
    "source": "Cleasby-Vigfusson, An Icelandic-English Dictionary, s.v. fen, vegr",
    "confidence": 0.85
  }
]
